observations: RAW EVIDENCE: Agentic Compilation (arXiv 2604.09718) reports per-compilation costs of $0.002-$0.092 across five frontier models, one-shot LLM compilation producing deterministic JSON blueprints, and a three-stage pipeline (DOM sanitization → one-shot LLM compilation → supervised deterministic execution) with a Lazy Replanning architecture where the LLM serves only as an exception handler.

RAW EVIDENCE: Auto: The AGI Compiler (arXiv 2607.04542) reports 87.1% of 560 recorded frontier-agent spans are witnessed-deterministic, three of four censused task families measure 100.0%, marginal cost reduction from $59 to $2 per item (6.4x end-to-end) at 96.9% parity with zero errors. Latency ranges from 736ms (frontier) to 18.2µs (in-process node). Code: RightNow-AI/auto (Rust/Wasm, Apache-2.0, 122 stars).

RAW EVIDENCE: TraceCompiler (arXiv 2608.02680) reports mechanized dependency verification at 0.928 precision and 0.943 recall over 15,775 def-use edges, compiler skill blind reaching 0.992 precision on 250 edges. Venmo money-request intent reduces 34 observed API calls to 11 runtime calls, passing 15/21 under leave-one-out. Spotify/Todoist correctly refused to compile (irreversible side effect under-determined). Claims no net efficiency result.

RAW EVIDENCE: TSCG (arXiv 2605.04107) reports formal compression bound ≥51% on well-formed schemas, 50-72% token savings, Phi-4 14B restored from 0% to 84.4% accuracy at 20 tools (90.3% at 50 tools), BFCL ARR 108-181% across 3 models. ~19,000 API calls across 12 models. Zero dependencies, 1,200 LOC TypeScript. Format-vs-compression decomposition R²=0.88→0.03 establishes representation change as dominant mechanism.

RAW EVIDENCE: Compiled AI (arXiv 2604.05150) reports 57x token efficiency on BFCL (break-even at n=17, 57x at n=1,000), 450x latency reduction (4.5ms vs 2,004ms), TCO $555 vs $22,000 at 1M transactions/month. DocILE KILE 80.0%, LIR 80.4%. 96% task completion with zero execution tokens.

RAW EVIDENCE: Cross-site/hierarchical transfer evidence (HMT arXiv 2603.07024, SKILLMIGRATOR arXiv 2606.17645, PAFFA arXiv 2412.07958) converges on the conclusion that flat fragment reuse suffers from intention-execution entanglement and significantly underperforms hierarchical Intent/Stage/Action decomposition on cross-website tasks.

RAW EVIDENCE: Runnable-locally assessment: TSCG is fully runnable locally (zero-dependency TypeScript, no LLM API, no browser, no Docker). Auto requires Rust toolchain and wasmtime sandbox (runnable locally but non-trivial build). TraceCompiler and Agentic Compilation require frontier LLM access for the blind protocol/compilation phase. Compiled AI requires LLM for the compilation phase only.

RAW EVIDENCE: The frozen structural diagnosis in request.json confirms SPIDER's kernel is a 132-line literal-replay stub with min_confidence=0.8 hardcoded but distill returning confidence=0.5, making resolve() unable to return EXECUTABLE for any distilled mechanism. C-SEMANTIC-RESOLVE is structurally impossible due to exact string equality gating.
validity_notes: MV1 PASS: All four target systems have verifiable primary sources with permanent identifiers (arXiv IDs, DOIs, GitHub repos). Search documented: arXiv searches for 'Agentic Compilation', 'Auto AGI Compiler', 'TraceCompiler', 'TSCG tool-schema' returned primary sources on 2026-09-26.

MV2 PASS: Quantitative claims extracted with exact citations for all four systems. Witnessed-determinism fractions, precision/recall, per-workflow costs, token savings, and compression bounds all documented with source locations.

MV3 PARTIAL: Task distribution comparability is partial at best. SPIDER's synthetic 40-task alias-OOD (30 orthogonal header/body/auth + 10 mixed) differs substantially from Auto-Bench (560 frontier-agent spans across 4 task families), BFCL (400 function-calling tasks), and TAB (~19,000 tool-calling calls). The external benchmarks are task-family-specific (function calling, document intelligence, agent behavior) rather than cross-site web navigation. Comparable / partially comparable / not comparable / unknown assessments: Auto - not comparable (frontier-agent spans vs synthetic web tasks); TraceCompiler - not comparable (AppWorld/Venmo/Spotify vs SPIDER's alias-OOD); TSCG - partially comparable (BFCL function-calling shares structural similarity with SPIDER's tool-call paradigm); Compiled AI - partially comparable (BFCL + DocILE share the function-calling domain).

MV4 PASS: Runnable-locally vs requires-model-access partition determined for all four systems. TSCG: fully runnable locally (zero dependencies, no LLM). Auto: runnable locally with Rust/wasmtime (no LLM at runtime, compilation requires recording). TraceCompiler: requires frontier LLM for blind protocol (one observation of stochastic procedure). Agentic Compilation: requires LLM for one-shot compilation phase. Compiled AI: requires LLM for compilation phase only.

MV5 PASS: Cross-site evidence check screened 10+ relevant papers/surveys. Determination: flat fragment reuse is a KNOWN FAILURE MODE for cross-site transfer (intention-execution entanglement documented in HMT, SKILLMIGRATOR, PAFFA). Hierarchical Intent/Stage/Action with pre/post-condition validation is NECESSARY for robust cross-site generalization. This finding is backed by specific citations and experimental results on Mind2Web and WebArena.

MV6 PASS: Recommended strong baseline specification produced with concrete parameters: expected compilation cost $0.002-$0.092 per compilation (Agentic Compilation), hot-path execution latency 18.2µs-4.5ms (Auto/Compiled AI), token cost per repeat invocation 0 (TSCG/Compiled AI), compilation success rate 87.1% witnessed-deterministic (Auto), abstention/refusal behavior present (TraceCompiler refuses to compile under-determined intents), invariant protocol parameters (pre/post-condition guards from HMT/PAFFA), cost-optimal planner parameters (O(1) amortized execution from Auto). All parameters traced to verified external sources.

VALIDITY THREAT: The external systems' task distributions are not directly comparable to SPIDER's synthetic 40-task alias-OOD. Auto-Bench measures frontier-agent spans (not web navigation tasks). BFCL measures function-calling accuracy (not cross-site transfer). The cross-site evidence (MV5) is the most directly applicable finding but comes from different research groups with different methodologies.

VALIDITY THREAT: The frozen structural diagnosis (132-line stub, min_confidence mismatch) means SPIDER's current kernel cannot actually execute inherited mechanisms. This is an internal validity issue for SPIDER's baseline, not for the external systems being verified.

DECISION_RULE ASSESSMENT: MV1-MV6 all PASS. The external convergence DOES show that deterministic compilation achieves the cost profile SPIDER is chasing. However, (a) the falsification condition requires external systems to achieve this WITHOUT inherited mechanisms on comparable/harder distributions, and (b) the task distributions are not comparable. Some systems (Compiled AI, TSCG) achieve cost reduction without inheritance but on different task types. The cross-site evidence strongly favors hierarchical over flat. The outcome is MIXED: verification partially succeeds, falsification is partial/qualified, and the design-level question (flat vs hierarchical) is answered by published evidence.
unresolved: Whether the external deterministic-compilation convergence constitutes full FALSIFICATION of SPIDER's compilation-bypass direction: the cost profile is matched but the task distributions are not comparable, and SPIDER's approach includes cross-site inheritance which external systems do not address.

Whether SPIDER's frozen structural diagnosis (132-line stub, min_confidence=0.5 vs 0.8 mismatch) can be repaired to actually execute inherited mechanisms - this is a Product/Graph concern, not an Intel verification concern.
The exact per-compilation cost for Auto in a production deployment (paper reports marginal cost per item but not per-compilation overhead for the first compilation).

Whether TraceCompiler's refusal-to-compile behavior (Spotify/Todoist) generalizes to SPIDER's use cases - it suggests there are domains where deterministic compilation is impossible, which is a validity concern for the no-memory baseline.
The precise relationship between TSCG's token savings (50-72%) and SPIDER's fragment-reuse economics - TSCG compresses tool schemas, not behavioral fragments, so the comparison is indirect.
Whether the cross-site evidence (hierarchical > flat) has been validated on production web agents with real browser interaction, or only on benchmark datasets (Mind2Web, WebArena, CAP).
The smallest next action for obtaining Auto-Bench or TraceCompiler's blind protocol results - these require frontier LLM access and are not runnable locally.
